maria: Quick status from the int8 bring-up across regions — ran a 2h soak comparing PCIe (gpc-pcie-usw) vs SXM (gpc-sxm-use) with our int8 kernel set. Observed consistent p50 parity but p95 on PCIe nodes in us-west is ~20% higher. Suspect NVLink hop + NUMA pinning interaction when requests cross the CPU boundary. :thinking:
josh: Can you paste the numbers and the exact runner flags you used?
maria: Yup. Command used: ```./bench_runner --model ocp-7b --quant int8 --nodes 4 --batch 4 --seq 1024 --kernel int8_fast_kv --pin-strategy auto --warmup 200```
perf-bot: job 1733333333 completed — artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/1733333333/ (metrics.csv, traces.zip) :white_check_mark:
maria: Attached the key CSV lines here: ``region,node_type,p50_ms,p95_ms,throughput_rps
us-west,pcie,18.6,48.2,210
us-east,sxm,18.2,40.1,225
europe,pcie,19.1,46.5,200
europe,sxm,18.7,39.8,215``
liam: Interesting. So p50 roughly same but p95 gap only on pcie-us-west. Were these nodes mixed-sku or homogeneous? Any leftover processes?
maria: Homogeneous runs. Node config: 8x A100-80GB (PCIE) in west, 8x A100-80GB (SXM) in east. Kernel selection was identical but runtime picked slightly different CUDA kernels due to topology heuristics.
sophia: Did you check the CPU->GPU affinity map? NVLink bridging can cause an extra memcpy if the KV cache lands on a different NUMA zone. Can you paste `nvidia-smi topo -m` and `numactl --hardware` snap?
maria: Copied snippet: ``nvidia-smi topo -m
GPU0 GPU1 GPU2 GPU3 CPU aff
GPU0 X NVLINK NVLINK PCIe node0
GPU1 NVLINK X NVLINK PCIe node0
GPU2 NVLINK NVLINK X PCIe node1
GPU3 PCIe PCIe PCIe X node1`` and `numactl --hardware` shows nodes 0/1 with CPU sockets split. So when a request touches KV that lives on GPU2/3, we see an extra XCOPY path across CPU nodes.
josh: That explains the tail. Suggest try strict pinning to keep model + KV on same NUMA node: `numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0` + set `--gpu-affinity 0,1,2,3` accordingly. Also test `--kernel int8_kv_eager` vs `int8_fast_kv` to see if the kernel path trades latency for throughput.
liam: Also try disabling cross-node NVLink piggybacking — force local GPU placement with the routing policy: `--route-policy local_pref` to avoid fallback to remote GPU for cold KV hits.
maria: Ran two quick follow-ups (small runs): ``test A = pinned numa0 + int8_kv_eager -> us-west p95 41.8ms (down from 48.2)
test B = pinned numa0 + int8_fast_kv -> p95 43.0ms`` So eager kernel helped more than fast_kv here. Throughput dropped ~6% on eager.
sophia: Good signal. Could be the fast_kv path is optimized for contiguous KV access across NVLink but when crossing CPU boundary it hits an unexpected memcpy hotspot. We should capture a perf trace: use `--tracing perf` and collect a few tails.
maria: I'll queue a 30-min trace run with `--trace perf --trace-sample p95` and upload. Also filing a perf ticket: PERF-4870 with the artifacts and the `nvidia-smi topo` maps.
josh: For rollout guidance — recommend we ship an operator knob: `force_local_numapinning` default off, enabled for PCIe clusters in west until we resolve kernel mismatch. Add a regression test in CI that runs a tiny p95 check on both topologies.
liam: One more ask: can we reproduce this on dedicated (reserved) capacity vs hosted? If reserved shows same gap then it's likely kernel/runtime; if only hosted it's a scheduling/VM placement artifact.
maria: Good call. I'll run dedicated cluster sweep tomorrow. Action items: 1) upload perf traces (maria), 2) try kernel override + pinning (maria), 3) add operator knob PR (josh), 4) CI p95 smoke (liam).
sophia: Thanks — ping when traces are up, cc @eng-runtime. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
maria: Uploaded traces and linked PERF-4870, leaving raw traces at s3 path in ticket. Will follow up with a small reproducer script. Thanks all. :rocket:
